name: Festung Kufstein
kurzbeschreibung: Festung Kufstein towers over a 90 m cliff: first documented in 1205, Kaiserturm by Maximilian I., Heldenorgel, and Panoramabahn.
beschreibung:
Overview

The monumental Festung Kufstein rises on a 90-meter-high, steep dolomite rock in the center of the historic border town of Kufstein on the Inn River. As a landmark visible from afar, the impressive defensive fortress looks back on more than eight centuries of eventful Tyrolean and Bavarian history. Today, the fortress is among the most visited sights in western Austria, delighting cultural travelers with historic exhibition rooms, spectacular ramparts, modern museums, and top-tier cultural events set against the backdrop of the Kaisergebirge mountains.

History & Architecture

First recorded in 1205 as castrum Caofstein in the joint possession of the Bishops of Regensburg and the Bavarian dukes, the border stronghold was fiercely contested for centuries. In 1504, Habsburg Emperor Kaiser Maximilian I. besieged the town and conquered the fortress for Tyrol following massive artillery bombardment with the famous giant cannons Purlepaus and Weckauf. Maximilian recognized its strategic value and expanded the stronghold into an impregnable imperial state fortress: from 1518, the mighty Kaiserturm was built – a monumental round tower standing 30 meters high with walls up to seven and a half meters thick. In the 18th and 19th centuries, the Kaiserturm served the Habsburgs as a notorious state prison for Hungarian freedom fighters and Italian insurgents. A worldwide rarity is the Heldenorgel, installed in 1931: with 4,948 pipes, it is the largest outdoor organ in the world, whose music resonates up to ten kilometers across the Unterinntal under favorable wind conditions. Further highlights of the tour include the 60-meter-deep Tiefe Brunnen well, the casemates, the torture chamber in the Fuchsturm, and the underground rock passage.

Visit & Getting There

Festung Kufstein is open daily year-round: during the summer season (April to October) daily from 09:00 to 18:00 (last admission at 17:00), in the winter months from 10:00 to 17:00. The daily organ recital of the Heldenorgel takes place at 12:00 noon (with an additional performance at 18:00 in July and August). Admission prices (2025/2026 season): adults €15.00 (summer) / €13.50 (winter), youths/students €11.00, children aged 6 to 16 €8.50 / €7.50, family ticket €34.00 / €30.00. Ascent and descent via the modern inclined lift Panoramabahn Kaiser Maximilian is included in the ticket price. Getting there by train: from the international Kufstein railway station, it is just a five-minute walk across the Inn bridge directly to the valley station of the Panoramabahn. By car: Inntalautobahn A12 (Kufstein Nord or Süd exit), parking is available in the central parking garages Kultur Quartier or Arkadenplatz.

Tips

Thanks to the Panoramabahn Kaiser Maximilian and wheelchair-accessible elevators, the upper castle courtyard, the fortress restaurant, and selected exhibition areas are accessible without barriers; stairs must be negotiated for the historic defensive towers and casemates. Visitors should linger on the fortress terraces or in the castle garden promptly at 12:00 noon to experience the impressive acoustic volume of the Heldenorgel live. The fortress tavern serves refined Tyrolean cuisine accompanied by panoramic views.
